source_proposition_coverage.coverage_result: Ten material propositions represented in ten source clauses. E008 is source-separate controlled test, not an inferred write compromise in the real apps. No overlapping second incident allocated.
limitations: Claroc's exact 43,551 attempted addresses versus 43,601 discovered names may reflect different populations but is not reconciled by original raw logs.
Causally distinct app-publication and generated membership-control mechanisms share a product and report; publication controls are provider/user-side, not model autonomous choice.

Reviewed recognition clauses and exclusions for current published FC-089 and FC-090, and tested FC-083 against the generated membership check; primary and two secondaries are provisional AI assessments only.
FC-089 applies to directly observed protected information, not all no-sign-in apps. FC-090 specifically to password-bearing browser-delivered code; validity/unverified later use is not claimed.
FC-083 is confined to Claroc's synthetic test where the membership control was configured and run after automatically enrolling the user; its observable protective effect was inadequate.
Nearby FC-002 Capability-Authority Separation was not asserted: no model-side inference from technical reachability into authorisation was shown for the sharing-architecture issue.
Provider publication choice, user publication and post-notification takedown were assessed as context-only; no positive model mapping was added for human defensive controls.
All classes of the 82-class published taxonomy have not been formally retested against this record. No claim of exhaustive negative-class finding or human verification.

limitations: Reviewed 12 HIM 1.1.0 dimensions, specific-consequence pathway. Assigned S4 privacy for confirmed externally reachable highly sensitive patient clinical information, separate from the app-count statistic; no assumption of mass confirmed victim disclosure.
The directly measured 35,578 live no-login app count is not a count of private records or affected people. 650–800 is a sample-derived estimate of apps with private material.
Only synthetic test app records were changed. No verified edit or physical damage to real third-party data; property-asset-damage remains unreported.
No evidence sufficient to score realised financial loss, account misuse, patient clinical harm, psychological or other downstream harm. Unknown consequence is not S1.
Later comprehensive remediation, sensitive-data copy retention, disclosure duration and impacted-person counts remain unknown; higher/other harms not inferred.

retained_decisions.rationale: Independent team-list access rule established by user's four-person instruction; demonstrably uninvited sign-in obtained access and modification. 'Not aligned' with that bounded security-control proposition, voluntary framework only.
Directly observed client-delivered plaintext password-bearing records outside secret custody. Distinct protected authenticator-content obligation, not claimed account compromise.

excluded_candidate_reasons: NIST SC-8 transmission confidentiality: no organisation-selected protected transmission property or defective transmission control is evidenced, as distinct from intentionally public app page exposure.
NIST SC-28 information at rest: original storage, organisation-defined selected information-at-rest controls and effective state are not shown.
NIST AC-6 least privilege: the separate task-necessary assignment for the user and process is not fully represented; four-person authorisation is better directly tested through AC-3.
NIST IA-5(a) initial authenticator distribution: the episode is public code delivery, not a documented initial authenticator issuance to an authorised recipient.
NIST IA-5(h) individually specified authenticator protection controls: owner-selected individual or device controls are not established by the incident packet.
No ISO/IEC 27001 binding/conformance finding; primary exact edition or affected organisation policy scope is not independently verified.
OWASP application security frameworks supply topical security guidance but do not themselves establish that this operator has a specific legal duty; no unrelated automatic requirement row.
